dish: Shellfish-only menu: 25-35 kinds of seasonal shellfish (grilled, steamed, sashimi) from around Japan and Okinawa
n: Sakaemachi Kai Senmon Sakaba Hiikiya (栄町貝専門酒場 ひいき屋)
w: A red-lantern counter bar in Sakaemachi Market that serves only shellfish. It usually has 25 or more kinds of seasonal shellfish from around Japan and Okinawa, rising past 35 at peak season. The counter faces the market lane, and Tabirai describes it as a place where you easily get talking to locals ('ichariba chōdē').

dish: Kokutō (black-sugar) zenzai: Okinawa shaved ice over kintoki beans with seasonal-fruit syrups, e.g. the strawberry 'ichigo daifuku' zenzai
n: Okinawa Kokutō Zenzai Senmonten Hoshi no Shizuku, Matsuo (沖縄 黒糖ぜんざい専門店 ホシのシズク)
w: A black-sugar zenzai specialist on the Heiwa/Taihei-dōri shopping arcade side of Kokusai-dōri, opened in September 2023. It serves Okinawa-style zenzai, fluffy shaved ice over sweet kintoki beans and black-sugar syrup, with toppings made from seasonal produce gathered from around the prefecture.

dish: Gōyā champurū and Okinawa soba with nightly shima-uta and sanshin shows and Ryūkyū folk dance
n: Okinawa Jiryōri Hateruma, Kokusai-dōri (沖縄地料理 波照間 国際通り店)
w: A min'yō izakaya in the middle of Kokusai-dōri with red-tile-roofed booths. Island-song and sanshin sets plus Okinawan folk-dance performances run at 18:30, 20:00 and 21:00, served alongside Okinawa soba and champurū. Japan's national tourism site points to it for nightly sanshin music on Kokusai-dōri.

dish: 'Hole Star' (a round bread made with tapioca flour) and 'Nouvelle' sponge-cake bread
n: Kameshima Pan, Nichūmae (かめしまパン 二中前店)
w: A branch of Kameshima Pan, a long-established Naha bakery, facing Naha High School (the old 'Ni-chū', Second Middle School). It has traded here for close to 40 years, opens at 6 am, and has about 60 breads set out by 8:30. Students buy the chewy tapioca-flour 'Hole Star' and the sponge-like 'Nouvelle'. Ryukyu Shimpo profiled the shop's history in its 'eating in front of the high school' series.
